notes.meaning: Israel fell back into worshiping idols, so God let the Philistines rule over them for forty years. The Philistines were a warlike coastal people who severely troubled the land. Unlike earlier times, the people did not even cry out to God for help, showing how hardened they had become in their sin.

A man named Manoah lived in Zorah, a town belonging to the tribe of Dan near the Philistine border. His wife was unable to have children, which was considered a deep sorrow in ancient times. God often chose mothers who were barren to bring about remarkable new beginnings for His people.

The angel of the Lord appeared to Manoah's wife with surprising news. He acknowledged her sadness at being childless and promised that she would soon give birth to a son. This heavenly messenger brought comfort right when the family and the nation felt their troubles most deeply.

The messenger warned the woman not to drink wine or any strong drink, and not to eat food that the law called unclean. Because the baby inside her was chosen for a special sacred calling, she had to practice these holy rules during her pregnancy. A mother's quiet choices can have a lasting impact on her child.

The angel told her that the boy was to be a Nazirite, someone specially dedicated to God, for his entire life. As a physical sign of this sacred promise, his hair was never to be cut. God planned for this boy to take the first steps in rescuing Israel from Philistine oppression.

The woman hurried to tell her husband that a man sent from God had visited her. She described him as having an awesome and majestic appearance, much like an angel. She felt so overwhelmed by his presence that she did not ask where he came from or what his name was.

She repeated the visitor's promise that she would have a son and shared the strict dietary rules she must follow. She stressed that the boy's special dedication to God would last from before birth until the day he died. She trusted the message completely and wanted her household to be ready.

Manoah did not doubt the heavenly promise, but he prayed asking God to send the messenger back. He wanted clear instructions on how they should raise and care for the promised child. Faithful parents turn to God in prayer for wisdom to guide their children.

God kindly answered Manoah's prayer and sent the messenger again. The angel appeared to the woman while she was sitting alone out in the field without her husband. This showed God's willingness to give guidance to those who honestly seek it.

As soon as she saw the visitor, the woman ran quickly to find her husband. She told Manoah that the very same person who had spoken to her earlier had returned. Her fast reaction showed her excitement and her desire for Manoah to meet him too.

Manoah followed his wife back out to the field to meet the visitor. When he arrived, he asked if this was the same person who had spoken to his wife, and the messenger confirmed that he was. Manoah approached him with great respect and an eager desire to learn.

Manoah expressed his faith that the promise would surely come true and asked about the boy's future way of life. He wanted to know what specific rules they must observe and what the boy's mission would be. He was eager to do his fatherly duty well.

The angel answered by pointing Manoah back to the instructions already given to his wife. Instead of describing Samson's future exploits, the Lord kept the focus on simple obedience. God often calls His people to fulfill their present duties rather than trying to figure out the future.

The messenger repeated that the mother must avoid anything from grapevines, wine, strong drink, and unclean food. She was commanded to obey everything God told her to do. Faithfulness in small, practical matters is essential when serving the Lord.

Manoah urged the visitor to stay awhile so they could prepare a young goat for him to eat. In the ancient world, preparing a good meal was an important way to show honor and hospitality to a guest. Manoah still thought he was speaking with a human prophet sent from God.

The angel stated that he would not eat any earthly food, but said that Manoah could offer a burnt sacrifice directly to the Lord. Manoah still did not realize that his visitor was heavenly and divine. True messengers of God always redirect worship away from themselves and toward the Lord.

Manoah asked the visitor for his name so that they could honor him when his words came true. It was common practice to give gifts and praise to prophets who brought good tidings. Manoah wanted to be sure the messenger received proper gratitude for his help.

The angel asked why Manoah inquired about his name, explaining that it was too wonderful and beyond human comprehension. The name showed that the messenger's nature was divine and mysterious. God's full greatness is beyond what our human minds can completely grasp.

differ.view: Many evangelicals believe this visitor was the Son of God appearing before His human birth, because His name 'wonderful' matches the title of Christ in Isaiah 9:6.

notes.meaning: Manoah placed the young goat and a grain offering on a large rock to sacrifice them to the Lord. As the couple watched, the Lord performed an astonishing miracle before their eyes. The ordinary rock became a holy place where God displayed His divine power.

As the flame leaped up from the rock toward the sky, the angel ascended into the fire toward heaven. Seeing this amazing sign, Manoah and his wife fell flat on the ground with their faces in the dirt. God revealed His holy presence in a way that left them filled with awe.

The angel vanished into the flame and was not seen by them again. Through this incredible miracle, Manoah finally realized that their visitor was the angel of the Lord. Their eyes were opened to the supernatural reality of God's presence among them.

Manoah was terrified and told his wife that they were surely going to die because they had seen God. Ancient Israelites knew that sinful human beings could not look directly upon God's holiness and live. His sudden dread shows how deeply he felt his own human unworthiness.

Manoah's wife comforted him with clear, sensible faith. She pointed out that if the Lord planned to destroy them, He would not have accepted their sacrifice, shown them miracles, or given them such wonderful promises. Remembering God's past mercies helps calm our deepest fears.

In due time, the woman gave birth to a baby boy and gave him the name Samson. The child grew up under the special favor and blessing of the Lord. God proved Himself completely faithful to the promise He had made.

As Samson grew, the Holy Spirit began to stir him with great courage and strength in the camp of Dan. These inner impulses prepared him for his future task of standing up against the Philistine oppressors. God gives His Spirit to equip His people for the work He calls them to do.
